about: Full bank of 200 benchmark questions (the 45 in benchmark_questions.json were chosen from these). Same format.

groups.fact: one fact from one official PDF, asked in farmer-style words
groups.multi_case: answer has 2+ cases that differ (e.g. kharif vs rabi)
groups.language: Hindi / Kannada / Nepali / Hinglish / romanised Kannada / typos
groups.reply_language: English question, but the user chose another language for the answer
groups.false_premise: question assumes something the PDFs contradict -- the app must correct it
groups.not_in_docs: on-topic, but the answer is not in the PDFs -- must give honest general guidance
groups.off_topic: sports, movies, coding, tricks to break the rules -- must be refused

questions.q: I have a KCC crop loan but I don't want PMFBY insurance this kharif. Till when should I tell the bank that I want to opt out?
questions.reference: A loanee farmer can opt out any time during the year by giving a written declaration to the bank branch, but at least 7 days before the cut-off date for enrolment for that season.
questions.evidence: any time during the year but at least seven days prior to the cut-off date for enrolment of farmers for the respective season

questions.q: last year i gave opt out form to bank for fasal bima. this season also will they keep me out or will they enroll me again?
questions.reference: The opt-out applies only for the season it was given; for the current season the bank will enrol the farmer automatically unless he submits a fresh opt-out form for this season too.
questions.evidence: he will be enrolled automatically for the current season by the bank branch as a normal process

questions.q: During the insurance contract period, how much can the sum insured for a crop be increased from one year to the next because of change in scale of finance or MSP?
questions.reference: Any change in the sum insured over a year due to changes in scale of finance / farm gate price is capped at 10% within the contract period.
questions.evidence: will be capped at 10% within the contract period

questions.q: How do they calculate the threshold yield for my crop in our village under crop insurance? How many years of data is taken?
questions.reference: Average yield is the average of the best 5 years out of the last 7 years for the crop in the insurance unit; threshold yield = this average yield multiplied by the notified indemnity level (70%, 80% or 90%).
questions.evidence: The Average Yield of a notiﬁed crop in IU will be the average yield of the best ﬁve years out of the last seven years.

questions.q: Wild boars and elephants keep destroying my crops. If our state gives the wild animal attack add-on cover, who has to pay its premium? Will central government subsidy be there?
questions.reference: The wild-animal add-on is optional and its premium is borne in full by the farmer; Central Government premium subsidy is not available for it, though the State/UT may give additional subsidy.
questions.evidence: The Central Govt. subsidy on premium shall not be available for this add-on cover.

questions.q: Bank has my KCC loan for soybean but now I want to sow maize instead. Up to when can I inform the bank to change the insured crop?
questions.reference: A loanee farmer can change the insured crop by informing the bank branch in writing up to 2 working days before the cut-off date for enrolment, provided the new crop is also notified.
questions.evidence: to the concerned bank branch up to 2 working days before the cut-off date for enrolment

questions.q: My PMFBY application was rejected by the insurance company. Will I get my premium back and within how many days?
questions.reference: Yes. The premium for a rejected application must be refunded to the farmer's bank account within 45 days of closure of the cut-off date for uploading of data, otherwise the insurance company must accept the application and pay claims.
questions.evidence: must be refunded back to the farmer's bank account within 45 days of closure of cut-off date for uploading of data by Banks

questions.q: There was no rain at sowing time and in our whole area we could not sow at all. If prevented sowing is declared, how much claim do we get and does the insurance continue after that?
questions.reference: Under prevented sowing the payout is 25% of the sum insured, and the insurance cover for that crop then gets terminated (no further claims for that crop/IU).
questions.evidence: The amount payable would be 25% of the gross total Sum Insured and the insurance coverage shall get terminated.

questions.q: After the state government notifies prevented sowing in our area, within how many days must the insurance company pay the claim?
questions.reference: The insurance company must disburse the prevented sowing claim within 30 days of the State/UT notification invoking the event.
questions.evidence: The Insurance Companies shall disburse the claim within 30 days of the State/UTs Notiﬁcation invoking the event of the insured risk.

questions.q: Severe dry spell in the middle of the season, crop looks very bad. Can we get some advance claim money before harvest, and how much?
questions.reference: Yes, under the mid-season adversity cover an 'on-account' payment of 25% of the likely claims is paid (if expected yield is below 50% of normal yield), adjusted later against final yield-based claims.
questions.evidence: Amount payable would be 25% of the likely claims subject to adjustment against ﬁnal yield claims

questions.q: My harvested crop was lying in the field to dry and got spoiled by unseasonal rain. How much rain is needed for post-harvest loss claim to trigger?
questions.reference: Post-harvest loss due to unseasonal rain is triggered when the unseasonal rainfall is more than 20% above the long period average for that month for the sub-district/district (and damage is confirmed in a joint survey).
questions.evidence: when the unseasonal rainfall is more than 20% over long period average for the month

questions.q: My paddy field got flooded and water stood for days. Can I claim under localized calamity for inundation?
questions.reference: No. The inundation peril under localized calamity is not applicable to hydrophilic crops like paddy, sugarcane, jute and mesta.
questions.evidence: Inundation peril is not applicable in the case of hydrophilic crops like Paddy, Sugarcane, Jute and Mesta.

questions.q: Suppose the insurance company is not able to transfer my claim because of bank account problems again and again. After how long does that money go away, and where?
questions.reference: If the claim cannot be remitted to the farmer for 6 consecutive seasons despite efforts to trace him, the claim amount is transferred to the FIAT account maintained by the Government of India.
questions.evidence: during 6 consecutive seasons despite due attempts and efforts have been made to trace the farmer

questions.q: My father had crop insurance and he passed away before the claim came. Can we get the claim money? What is needed?
questions.reference: Yes. The claim is paid to the legal heir after the insurance company updates the heir's bank account, subject to submission of a legal heir certificate and a declaration by the heir with bank details.
questions.evidence: subject to submission of legal heir certificate and certificate/declaration by the legal heir

questions.q: The CSC centre guy is asking Rs 100 extra over the premium to fill my PMFBY form. Is he allowed to take this?
questions.reference: No. CSC-VLEs must not demand any service charge or extra amount from farmers beyond the applicable premium; a VLE doing so shall be de-empanelled by CSC e-Gov and may face legal action.
questions.evidence: VLEs shall not demand any service charges or any extra amount from farmers other than the applicable premium amount.

questions.q: What service charge does a bank get from the insurance company for enrolling farmers under PMFBY?
questions.reference: Banks (including Banking Correspondents) are paid service charges at 4% of the farmer's share of premium by the insurance company for farmers enrolled by them.
questions.evidence: shall be paid service charges @ 4% of the farmer's share of premium by Insurance Company

questions.q: Our crop insurance dispute with the insurance company is worth about Rs 40 lakh. Do we have to start with the taluka grievance officer or can we go higher directly?
questions.reference: Grievances exceeding Rs 25 lakh (or affecting many districts / breach of guidelines) can be raised directly at the State Level Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC), which disposes of them within 15 days.
questions.evidence: the grievance matter exceeds Rs. 25 Lakh in monetary terms, such matters may be directly raised at the level of the State Level Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC)

questions.q: Under YES-TECH, what is the minimum weight given to technology-based yield in arriving at final crop yield?
questions.reference: YES-TECH provides a minimum 30% weightage (threshold) for technology-driven yield in the final crop yield value for approved crops.
questions.evidence: YES-TECH provides for minimum 30% threshold for technology driven yield

questions.q: How many people do we need at minimum to register a new co-operative society in Karnataka? Can my family members be the applicants?
questions.reference: Where all applicants are individuals there must be at least ten of them, each above 18 years of age, and they must not be members of the same family.
questions.evidence: where all the applicants are individuals, the number of applic ants shall not be less than ten;

questions.q: We submitted our registration application to the Registrar. How long can he take to decide, and what happens if he doesn't decide in time?
questions.reference: The Registrar must register the society within three months of receiving the application; if he fails to dispose of it within that period, the society and its bye-laws are deemed to be registered.
questions.evidence: If the Registrar is unable to dispose of such application within the period specified in sub -section (1), the society and the bye -laws shall be deemed to have been registered.

questions.q: i gave my membership application to our society long back and they are not replying. how much time do they have to decide? what if they never answer
questions.reference: The society must admit or refuse the applicant within two months of receiving the application and communicate it in writing; if no communication is received in that period, the application is deemed to have been accepted.
questions.evidence: Every co -operative society shall within 2 [two months ]2 from the date on which application for admission was delivered to such society either admit or refuse

questions.q: Our society refused to make me a member. Where can I appeal and within how many days?
questions.reference: An appeal against refusal of admission lies to the Registrar, by written petition within sixty days of the communication of refusal (or of the deemed refusal); the society must implement the Registrar's order within fifteen days.
questions.evidence: shall be made by a petition in writing within sixty days by the person seeking admission of the communication of refusal

questions.q: Is there any limit on how many associate members a co-op society can have in Karnataka?
questions.reference: Yes. Associate members (individuals) cannot exceed fifteen percent of the total membership of the society.
questions.evidence: the number of associate members under clause (a) in any Co -operative Society shall not exceed fifteen percent of the total membership o f the society.

questions.q: As secretary I need to know who picks the auditor for our society's accounts, and by when do we have to hand over the year's financial statements to the auditor?
questions.reference: The general body appoints the auditor or auditing firm from the panel approved by the Director of Co-operative Audit, and the board must present the annual financial statements to the auditor within thirty days of the close of the co-operative year.
questions.evidence: presented for audit before the auditor or auditing firm within thirty days of the closure of that cooperative year.

questions.q: Our co-operative society is registered in Karnataka. What is the last date by which we must hold our annual general meeting every year?
questions.reference: Every co-operative society must hold its annual general meeting once a year before the twenty-fifth day of September.
questions.evidence: Every co -operative society shall convene a general meeting of its members once in a year before 3 [twenty fifth day of September ]3

questions.q: Our society has around 25,000 members. What is the minimum quorum needed for the general body meeting?
questions.reference: Quorum is as per bye-laws but not less than one thousand members or ten percent of members eligible to vote, whichever is less; with about 25,000 members that means at least 1,000 members (the lower figure).
questions.evidence: not less than one thousand members or ten percent of the members eligible to vote whichever is less.

questions.q: I skipped most of the general body meetings in the last few years. Can the society stop me from voting? For how long?
questions.reference: Yes. A member who fails to attend three out of the last five general meetings (or fails to use the minimum services for three consecutive years) loses the right to vote at general meetings and board elections for a period of three years.
questions.evidence: a member, a representative or a delega te who has failed to attend three general meetings out of the last five general meetings;

questions.q: A group of us members want a special general meeting called. How many members must sign the request and how quickly does the board have to call it?
questions.reference: The board must call a special general meeting within one month of receiving a written requisition from the Registrar or from one-fifth of the total number of members.
questions.evidence: shall call such meeting within one month after the receipt of a requisition in w riting from the Registrar or from 2 [1 [XXX]2 one fifth of the total number of members

questions.q: We just got our society registered. Within how much time must we hold the first general meeting to elect the committee, and how long will that committee stay in office?
questions.reference: The first general meeting must be held within one month of registration to elect the first committee, and its term of office is five years from the date of election.
questions.evidence: first general meeting of a society after registration shall be held within one month from the date of its registration to elect the first committee

questions.q: One of our directors has not come to board meetings for months without informing anyone. Can he lose his post?
questions.reference: Yes. A person is disqualified from continuing as a board member if he has been absent for three consecutive board meetings without leave of absence.
questions.evidence: he has absented himself for three consecutive meetings of the board of such society , without leave of absence.

questions.q: If a director gives his resignation letter, from when does it become effective? can he take it back?
questions.reference: The resignation, addressed in writing to the Chief Executive, takes effect on expiry of fifteen days from the communication, unless the director withdraws it in writing within those fifteen days.
questions.evidence: it shall become vacant on the expiry of fifteen days from the date of such communication unless within the said period of fifteen days

questions.q: our society was registered last year but we never actually started any business. Can the Registrar close it down on his own?
questions.reference: Yes. The Registrar may on his own motion order winding up if the society has not commenced working within six months of registration or has ceased to function for six months.
questions.evidence: where the co -operative society has not commenced working 2 [within a period of six months of the date of its registration or has ceased to function for six months ]2

questions.q: The Registrar decided a dispute against me and ordered me to pay the society Rs 2 lakh. I want to appeal to the Tribunal. What is the time limit and do I have to pay anything first?
questions.reference: The appeal to the Tribunal must be filed within sixty days of the decision, and an appeal against an order for payment of money is considered only with proof of depositing twenty-five percent of the amount due with the society (here Rs 50,000).
questions.evidence: unless it is accompanied by satisfactory proof for having deposited with the concerned society twenty five percent of the amount due

questions.q: A private shop near our village calls itself 'Farmers Co-operative Store' but is not a registered society. Is that an offence, and what is the fine?
questions.reference: Yes. Any person other than a co-operative society using the word 'Co-operative' in its business name without State Government sanction is punishable with a fine up to two thousand rupees.
questions.evidence: without the sanction of the State Government, shall be punishable with a fine which may extend to 1 [two thousand]1 rupees.

questions.q: This season the state committee has not yet announced the scale of finance for my crop. How will the bank decide my KCC crop loan limit then?
questions.reference: If the SLTC has not notified the Scale of Finance for the season, the bank can apply a 10 per cent notional hike over the previous season's SoF to fix the drawing limit (if SoF is notified but not revised, the existing SoF is used).
questions.evidence: the bank shall consider applying a 10 per cent notional hike over the SoF applicable for the previous season

questions.q: I am a sharecropper, the landlord gives only oral lease and panchayat is not giving me any certificate. Can I still get KCC loan? upto how much?
questions.reference: Yes. If certification of a sharecropper/oral lessee is difficult, the bank shall accept the borrower's own affidavit about land tilled and crops grown, for loans up to Rs 50,000.
questions.evidence: banks shall accept an affidavit submitted by such borrowers giving their occupational status (i.e., details of land tilled / crops grown), for loans up to ₹50,000

questions.q: Our society has tie-up with a sugar factory which recovers the loan from cane payment and the crop is hypothecated. Up to what KCC amount can the bank skip collateral in this case?
questions.reference: For KCC loans against hypothecation of crops/stock with a tie-up arrangement for recovery, banks may waive collateral security for loans up to Rs 3 lakh.
questions.evidence: banks may waive collateral security for loans up to a limit of ₹3 lakh

questions.q: i grow a crop which is not in the district scale of finance list. will bank give it under kisan credit card?
questions.reference: No. Loans for crops not covered in the SoF finalised by the SLTC/DLTC are given outside the KCC framework, though efforts should be made to get the SoF for such crops notified.
questions.evidence: In respect of crops not covered in the SoF finalised by the SLTC / DLTC of the respective State, loans extended shall be outside the KCC framework

questions.q: Can the bank simply debit crop insurance or health insurance premium from my KCC account without asking me?
questions.reference: No. The KCC holder may choose to pay insurance premium through the KCC account, but the bank must take the farmer's explicit consent at the application stage itself; insurance funded under KCC is assigned in favour of the lending bank.
questions.evidence: Their explicit consent shall be obtained, at the application stage itself if the premium is to be paid through the KCC account.

questions.q: The bank calculated my KCC limit as Rs 93,480. Will they sanction exactly that or round it off?
questions.reference: The KCC credit limit is rounded off to the nearest Rs 1,000 (so about Rs 93,000 in this case).
questions.evidence: T he KCC credit limit shall be rounded off to the nearest ₹1,000.

questions.q: From which date do the new RBI KCC directions for rural cooperative banks apply to loans? What happens to KCC loans already sanctioned before that?
questions.reference: They apply to KCC loans sanctioned from January 01, 2027; loans sanctioned earlier continue under the existing guidelines until maturity or next renewal.
questions.evidence: The Directions shall be applicable to loans sanctioned under the KCC Scheme with effect from January 01, 2027.

questions.q: I have 3 acres farmland but I filed and paid income tax last year. Am I eligible for PM Kisan money?
questions.reference: No. Farmer families in which any member paid income tax in the last assessment year are excluded from PM-KISAN.
questions.evidence: v) All Persons who paid Income Tax in last assessment year.

questions.q: My husband is a practising doctor registered with the medical council and we own agricultural land in village. Can our family get PM-KISAN?
questions.reference: No. Families with a member who is a professional like a doctor, engineer, lawyer, CA or architect registered with a professional body and practising are excluded.
questions.evidence: Professionals like Doctors, Engineers, Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects registered with Professional bodies and carrying out profession by undertaking practices.

questions.q: I gave a complaint about my PM Kisan payment to the district grievance committee. Within how many days should they settle it?
questions.reference: Grievances or complaints should be disposed of on merit, preferably within two weeks.
questions.evidence: Any grievances or complaints which are received should be disposed off on merit preferably within two weeks time.

questions.q: If someone gave a wrong self declaration and took PM-KISAN money though not eligible, what will happen to him?
questions.reference: He will be liable for recovery of the financial benefit transferred to him and other penal action as per law.
questions.evidence: In case of incorrect self declaration, beneficiary shall be liable for recovery of transferred financial benefit and other penal actions as per law.

questions.q: Our temple trust owns 10 acres of cultivable land. Can the trust register for PM-KISAN benefit?
questions.reference: No. All institutional landholders are excluded from PM-KISAN; the scheme is only for landholding farmer families.
questions.evidence: The following categories of beneficiaries of higher economic status shall not be eligible for benefit under the scheme: (a) All Institutional Land holders

questions.q: I got drip irrigation subsidy on my survey number 4 years back. Now I want sprinkler on the same land, can I get PMKSY help again?
questions.reference: No. The same land parcel/survey number cannot get micro-irrigation support more than once within a 7-year window, so another subsidy is possible only after 7 years.
questions.evidence: The same unique land parcel or survey entity cannot access the micro-irrigation financial support loop more than once within a strict 7-year implementation window.

questions.q: I have 8 hectares. For how much area can I get Per Drop More Crop micro irrigation subsidy?
questions.reference: The maximum area per individual beneficiary registration is capped at 5 hectares.
questions.evidence: Max beneficiary cap is restricted to 5 hectares per individual registration.

questions.q: I am a farmer and want to become a full voting member of our new PACS. How many shares do I have to buy and how much will it cost me?
questions.reference: An individual must buy at least five shares of Rs 100 each, i.e. Rs 500, to become an A-class member (plus a non-refundable Rs 10 admission fee).
questions.evidence: Every individual shall subscribe at least five shares (Rs. 100/- each share) amounting to Rs. 500/ - of the Society to become an A -Class Member.

questions.q: how many directors can sit on the board of a PACS - what is the minimum and maximum?
questions.reference: Under the model bye-laws a PACS board has a minimum of 11 and a maximum of 21 members.
questions.evidence: There shall be minimum 11 and maximu m 21 members in the Board of Directors.

questions.q: Are any seats on the PACS board kept aside for women and SC/ST members? How many?
questions.reference: Yes. The model bye-laws reserve 2 seats for women and 1 seat for a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe member on the board.
questions.evidence: Reserva tion will be provided for 2 women and 1 Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes member in the Board.

questions.q: I gave my membership form to the society secretary long back and nothing has happened. Within how much time must the board decide on my application?
questions.reference: The CEO places the application before the Board, which must decide within a maximum of 6 months from receipt; the applicant is informed within 15 days of the board meeting, and a refusal can be appealed to the Registrar.
questions.evidence: who shall decide within a maximum period of 6 months from the date of receipt of application

questions.q: My son is 19 and a member of our cooperative society. Can he stand for election to the board of directors?
questions.reference: No. A person below 21 years of age is not eligible for election to the PACS Board of Directors.
questions.evidence: No person shall be eligible for election as a member of the Board of Directors of the Society if he: (a) is below 21 years of age

questions.q: One director in our PACS never comes to board meetings. After how many missed meetings does he lose his post?
questions.reference: A director who is absent from three consecutive board meetings without the Board's permission ceases to be a board member (the Board may reinstate him once on written request).
questions.evidence: If a Director of the Board absents himself from three consecutive meetings of the Board without the permission of the Board, he shall cease to be member of such Board.

questions.q: Can our PACS give a higher interest rate on deposits than the district cooperative bank? how much more is allowed?
questions.reference: PACS can accept deposits only from members, and the interest rate cannot be more than 2% above the DCCB's corresponding deposit rate.
questions.evidence: interest rate of deposits shall not be more than 2% over the corresponding deposit interest rate of DCCB

questions.q: Our PACS has become a Common Service Centre. Roughly how many kinds of online services can we offer to villagers through it?
questions.reference: Under the MoU with MeitY, NABARD and CSC e-Governance Services, PACS can provide more than 300 e-services such as banking, insurance, Aadhaar, PAN card and ticket booking.
questions.evidence: for providing more than 300 e -services such as banking, insurance, Aadhar enrolment/ updation, health services, PAN card

questions.q: Our society wants to open a petrol pump. Under which category can a PACS apply for a retail petrol/diesel outlet?
questions.reference: PACS have been included in Combined Category 2 (CC2) for allotment of retail petrol/diesel outlets.
questions.evidence: The Government has allowed PACS to be included in the Combined Category 2 (CC2) for allotment of retail petrol/ diesel outlets.

questions.q: Is a PACS allowed to take an LPG gas agency (distributorship)?
questions.reference: Yes. The Government has allowed PACS to apply for LPG distributorships so they can diversify their income.
questions.evidence: The Government has now allowed PACS to apply for LPG Distributorships.

questions.q: For building a godown under the grain storage plan with AMI scheme, how much margin money does the PACS have to put in now?
questions.reference: The margin money requirement under the AMI scheme has been reduced from 20% to 10%.
questions.evidence: the margin money requirement has been reduced from 20% to 10%

questions.q: Up to what amount can a PACS member deposit or receive cash in a day without income tax trouble? I heard the limit was only 20,000.
questions.reference: The limit for cash deposits and payments (and for cash loans/repayments) by PACS has been raised from Rs 20,000 to Rs 2 lakh per member.
questions.evidence: enhanced the limit for Cash Deposits and Payments by PACS and Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (PCARDBs) from Rs. 20,000 to Rs. 2 lakh per member

questions.q: A multi-state cooperative already has 21 elected directors. Can it still add experts like bankers to the board, and how many?
questions.reference: Yes. The board may co-opt experts (banking, management, finance etc.), but not more than two in addition to the 21 directors; co-opted directors cannot vote in office-bearer elections.
questions.evidence: the number of such co-opted members shall not exceed two in addition to twenty-one directors specified in this sub-section.

questions.q: I complained to the Co-operative Ombudsman about my deposit stuck in a multi state society. How long does the ombudsman have to decide my complaint?
questions.reference: The Co-operative Ombudsman must complete the inquiry and adjudicate within three months of receiving the complaint; the society must comply with its directions within one month.
questions.evidence: complete the process of inquiry and adjudicate within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the complaint

questions.q: I asked my multi-state society for information about its affairs. Within how many days must they reply, and where can I appeal if they reject it?
questions.reference: The Co-operative Information Officer must give the information or reject the application within 30 days; a rejected member can appeal to the Co-operative Ombudsman within one month.
questions.evidence: The Co-operative Information Officer shall, within thirty days from the date of receipt of application, either provide the information or reject the application

questions.q: If directors of a multi-state cooperative use the society's assets for their own personal gain, what punishment can they get?
questions.reference: They can be punished with imprisonment of at least one month up to one year, or a fine of Rs 5,000 up to Rs 1 lakh, or both, and the unlawful gains are recovered from them.
questions.evidence: such directors or officers concerned shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one month but which may extend to one year

questions.q: We cut our paddy and left it spread in the field to dry, then unseasonal rain came. For how many days after harvest is such crop covered under PMFBY?
questions.reference: Post-harvest losses are covered for up to a maximum of 14 days from harvesting for crops kept in 'cut and spread' condition to dry, against cyclone/cyclonic rain and unseasonal rain.
questions.evidence: Coverage is available upto a maximum period of 14 days from harvesting

questions.q: Rain failed badly and most farmers in our area could not even sow. Is there any claim for this under the crop insurance scheme and how much?
questions.reference: Yes. If most insured farmers of the notified area are prevented from sowing due to adverse weather, they can get indemnity up to a maximum of 25% of the sum insured.
questions.evidence: shall be eligible for indemnity claims upto a maximum of 25% of the sum-insured

questions.q: how is threshold yield worked out for a crop in PMFBY? how many years average they take?
questions.reference: Threshold yield is the average yield of the last seven years, excluding up to two declared calamity years, multiplied by the indemnity level of the area.
questions.evidence: based on average yield of last seven years excluding two years of declared calamity if any, multiplied by the level of indemnity of the area

questions.q: For the accident insurance (PMSBY) that comes with the farmer package, how much premium is cut from my bank account per year, and how much does family get if I die in an accident?
questions.reference: The premium is Rs 12 per year per member, auto-debited from the savings account, and the accidental death cover is Rs 2 lakh.
questions.evidence: Premium : Rs.12/- per annum per member. The premium will be deducted from the account holder’s savings bank account

questions.q: I am in the PMJJBY life cover through my bank. Till what age will this cover continue?
questions.reference: The PMJJBY assurance ends on the annual renewal date on attaining age 55 (age nearest birthday), or earlier if the account is closed or has insufficient balance.
questions.evidence: On attaining age 55 years (age nearest birthday) on annual renewal date.

questions.q: There is long dry spell in the middle of season and crop looks very bad. Can we get some claim money before harvest? Any limit on it?
questions.reference: Yes, an on-account payment can be made for mid-season adversity, not exceeding 25% of likely claims, and only if the expected yield is likely to be less than 50% of normal yield.
questions.evidence: will decide about crops/ areas for which on account payment will be made, not exceeding 25% of likely claims

questions.q: If there is a huge disaster all over the country, how much loss do insurance companies bear under PMFBY and who pays the rest?
questions.reference: Insurers' liability is up to 350% of total premium collected or 35% of total sum insured (whichever is higher); losses beyond this are met equally (50:50) by the Central and State Governments.
questions.evidence: shall be upto 350% of total premium collected (farmer share plus Govt. subsidy) or 35% of total Sum Insured (SI)

questions.q: Weather insurance: if the insurance company feels the rainfall data given by the state is wrong, how many days do they get to object? What if they don't object in time?
questions.reference: The insurer must report any anomaly to the State department within 7 days of receiving the weather data (resolved within the next 7 days by the Arbitration Committee); data not objected to within 7 days is treated as accepted by the insurer.
questions.evidence: However, data with anomalies which is not reported within 7 days will be treated as accepted to insurance company.

questions.q: Under RWBCIS our village weather station was broken during the season. Then from where will they take rain data for our claim?
questions.reference: Data from the notified back-up weather station is used; if that is also unavailable, data from the nearest IMD station is used.
questions.evidence: In absence of availability of weather data from back-up AWS, weather data from nearest IMD station shall be used

questions.q: Do I have to inform the insurance company about my crop loss under the weather based insurance (RWBCIS), or is claim automatic?
questions.reference: For weather-based risks, farmers need not lodge a claim intimation; claims are calculated from actual weather station data. Intimation is needed only for add-on localised risks like hailstorm/cloudburst, which are assessed at individual farm level.
questions.evidence: For remaining risks losses are caused due to weather conditions and hence lodging of intimation for claims by insured farmers / designated agencies for such weather conditions is not essential.

questions.q: In the RWBCIS deficit rainfall example (strike 200 mm, strike-2 150 mm, exit 100 mm), the station recorded only 120 mm. What is the claim per hectare and for a farmer with 2 hectares?
